items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 1:1
items.html:
Direct light and reflected light, comprising 15 chapters
in which the 13 kinds of ten Sefirot are explained

Chapter 1
It contains two matters. 1. The ten Sefirot of direct light, which are four phases of coarseness in which the upper light expands for a coupling by striking. 2. These four phases operate equally in each and every illumination, from the head of the line to the end of the world of Assiya, with no difference between them.

We must understand the difference between the 13 kinds of ten Sefirot that the ARI brings in this part
Here we have found, in the words of the ARI, 13 kinds of the ten Sefirot, KHB TM, and we must know the difference between them. 1) Ten Sefirot KHB TM of direct light, brought here (in Chapter 1, Item 3). 2) Ten Sefirot KHB TM of reflected light, brought here (in Chapter 2, Items 1 and 2). 3) Ten Sefirot called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida, brought here (in Chapter 2, Item 3). 4) Ten Sefirot called root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall, brought here (in Chapter 2, Item 3). 5) Ten Sefirot KHB TM whose level is equal, brought here (in Chapter 3, Item 4). 6) Ten Sefirot KHB TM that emerge one above the other, brought here (in Chapter 4, Item 1). 7) Ten Sefirot KHB TM that emerge one below the other, such as the four Partzufim Aba, Ima, ZA and Nukva, brought here (in Chapter 5, Item 1, and in Chapter 6, Item 4). 8) Ten Sefirot KHB TM of the Rosh of the Partzuf, brought here (in Chapter 5, Item 2). 9) Ten Sefirot KHB TM of the Toch of the Partzuf, down to the Tabur, which are called HGT, brought here (in Chapter 5, Item 3). 10) Ten Sefirot KHB TM of the Sof of the Partzuf, from the Tabur downward, brought in Chapter 7, which are called NHY. 11) Ten Sefirot KHB TM called the four worlds Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira and Assiya, brought here (in Chapter 14, Items 1, 2 and 3). 12) Ten Sefirot KHB TM, which are the four Partzufim Aba, Ima, ZA and Nukva, called the ABYA of the world of Atzilut, brought here (in Chapter 15). 13) Ten Sefirot KHB TM called the particular ABYA, which exist in each and every Partzuf of the Partzufim of ABYA, where the Rosh of every Partzuf is the meaning of Keter, and from the Peh to the Chazeh is the meaning of Atzilut, and from the Chazeh to the Tabur is Beria, and from the Tabur downward is Yetzira and Assiya.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 1:2
items.html: And here we have before us 13 kinds of ten Sefirot, and all these 13 kinds are called by the same names, and they all amount to one and the same thing; and with all this, the difference between them is very great. And a prior understanding is required in order to understand well the difference in each and every kind, with its reason and its ground; and then it becomes possible to discern, in every place, which kind of ten Sefirot is being spoken of.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 1:3
items.html:
There is no degree in which there are not ten Sefirot of direct light
Now the ten Sefirot of the direct light, which are the four phases HB TM, together with their root, which is called Keter, have already been well explained (in Part 1, Page 6, Sub Header, “And the reason,” and in Inner Light, Part 3, Chapter 1, Item 9). And these ten Sefirot are contained in the light of Ein Sof itself; and since there is no renewal of light in any of the worlds except from Ein Sof, it follows from this that these four phases of direct light are present equally in each and every illumination, from the head of the line to the end of Assiya, without any distinction on their part at all, as above in the words of the ARI (Chapter 2, Item 3, and in Inner Light, ibid., Item 9).
